critical.issue: SuggestIn.date: Optional[date] and Extraction.date: Optional[date] reject any non-null ISO date with Pydantic error 'Input should be None'. Root cause: field name `date` shadows the imported `date` type in the class-body annotation → Pydantic v2 interprets the field as None-only. Impact: (1) UI 'Refresh suggestions from edited details' (receipt-refresh-suggestions) will 422 whenever a date is present, (2) AI-extracted receipt date is silently dropped to null on the analyze path (schema returned by LLM cannot round-trip through Extraction if it contains a real date). Fix: rename field to `receipt_date`, or annotate explicitly as `datetime.date`, or `date_: date = Field(alias='date')`. Reproduced with `SuggestIn(vendor='X', date='2025-01-10')` and same for `Extraction(date='2025-01-10')`. `ExpenseIn.date: date` (non-Optional) is fine.

rca of the issue: Pydantic v2 forward-ref/local-name resolution: In a BaseModel class body, an annotation `Optional[date]` on a field also named `date` triggers Pydantic to resolve the type reference to the field itself (or a placeholder) rather than the module-scope `datetime.date` class, effectively producing a None-only schema. Reproducer: `python -c "from receipt_expenses import SuggestIn; SuggestIn(vendor='X', date='2025-01-10')"` → validation error `Input should be None [type=none_required]`. Same for Extraction. ExpenseIn.date: date (non-Optional) is unaffected because Pydantic treats bare `date` as the required-type annotation successfully. Mitigation: rename the field or use `datetime.date` explicitly.
